items.desc: Foreign minister says Nepal and India are working to make the prime minister’s visit fruitful and result-oriented.

items.title: Narayani flood leaves Bharatpur school covered in mud
items.desc: Teachers and students are shovelling out classrooms after four days of rain, and flooding left the school covered in thick silt, with outside help yet to arrive.

items.title: Nepal’s call for climate justice was heard, foreign minister says
items.desc: Shisir Khanal says the country’s UN engagement strengthened its diplomatic position as it seeks climate finance and reconstruction support after the floods.

items.title: Flood damages iconic Dodhara Chandani suspension footbridge
items.desc: Damage to the third span of the 1.5-km footbridge has prompted authorities to inspect the structure and warn people against using the affected section.

items.title: Justices question chief justice over ‘middlemen’ and Rana’s detention
items.desc: At a five-hour full-court meeting, most of the bench pressed Manoj Kumar Sharma on why the Supreme Court is mired in controversy just four months into his tenure.

items.title: Four Nepali judokas eliminated in opening bouts
items.desc: Judokas, including sisters Nisha Shrestha and Devaki Maya Shrestha and brothers Vishesh BK and Vikas BK, lose their opening bouts in Nagoya.

items.title: US Supreme Court lets Trump resume deporting migrants to countries not their own
items.desc: The justices put on hold a lower-court ruling requiring migrants facing third-country deportation to be given notice and a chance to raise fears of persecution or torture.

items.title: AI can imitate our songs. Can it preserve them?
items.desc: As AI-generated music borrows from Nepali folk traditions, the people and cultural histories behind those songs risk being pushed aside.

items.title: Nepal set to miss SAFF Men’s Championship for the first time
items.desc: SAFF gave Nepal until September 30 to have its FIFA ban lifted. Nepal is now almost certain to miss the deadline.

items.title: Respect the human rights commission’s constitutional authority
items.desc: Reluctance to respect the NHRC weakens an institution meant to protect rights and ensure accountability.

items.title: If AI automates work, how will Nepal fund the state?
items.desc: A national AI strategy that treats employment, tax and remittance dependence as central is the only way to leverage AI without hollowing out the state’s ability to function.

items.title: A month after the flood, survivors have nowhere to go, no way to earn
items.desc: Relief has helped families through the immediate aftermath, but damaged roads, lost homes, closed schools and shattered livelihoods are making recovery harder.

items.title: Microfinance borrowers land on blacklist as sources dry up
items.desc: More than 21,500 small borrowers were blacklisted in the last fiscal year, raising concerns that a system created to bring finance to poor households is leaving some of its most vulnerable users out of formal credit.

items.title: Civil Service Bill retains one-time retirement at 55 or after 30 years’ service
items.desc: The bill, approved for submission to Parliament, has been revised to ensure employees retired under the provision do not lose pension benefits after the Public Service Commission raised legal concerns.

items.title: In Nepal’s premium rental market, the dollar is everywhere but on paper
items.desc: Apartments and homes are increasingly listed in US dollars, edging out Nepali renters and operating in a legal gray zone that no regulator has ever tested.

items.title: NDRRMA Chief Upreti on what Nepal must change after the Bhotekoshi disaster
items.desc: A month after the Bhotekoshi flood, Nepal’s disaster authorities are assessing the damage, planning reconstruction and considering the relocation of settlements in high-risk areas.

items.title: Punya Prasad Sitaula on when Dashain ticket bookings could open
items.desc: The transport federation chair says bookings will depend on road conditions and safer routes for passengers.

items.title: US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving an opening for Iran
items.desc: While the eventual departure of US forces is broadly popular among Iraqis, those who worry about the strength of the Iran-backed groups fear the withdrawal is premature.

items.title: Is Nepal’s tourism industry moving fast enough?
items.desc: Nepal’s tourism recovery no longer needs to take years. By shifting from desperate emotional pleas to targeted, transparent digital storytelling, the industry can accelerate its rebound.

items.title: BP Highway reopens after five-day disruption
items.desc: Traffic resumed Tuesday morning on an under-construction permanent track after floods damaged the highway at eight locations.

items.title: Government revives failed plan to separate household and commercial LPG
items.desc: New committee will study separate cylinder sizes and prices for household and commercial users after the latest LPG shortage. Similar efforts in 2011 and 2013 were never implemented.

items.title: Machinery deployed to clear blocked Marsyangdi river in Chame
items.desc: Authorities are widening the river channel to protect homes and a motorable bridge threatened by the rising flow.

items.title: Public Service Commission raises objections to civil service bill provisions, prompting revisions
items.desc: Commission objects to proposed 55-year or 30-year service retirement rule and pension changes, saying they could conflict with legal protections for civil servants.

items.title: Major highways linking Kathmandu reopen after rain disruptions
items.desc: Traffic is flowing on the BP, Prithvi, Kanti, Tribhuvan and Arniko highways, though some sections remain restricted to one-way movement.

items.title: OpenAI shelves new AI model release over safety concerns
items.desc: The ChatGPT maker halted plans for its next-generation model after internal tests found it fell short of safety and alignment standards, including concerns over oversight and disclosure of its actions.

items.title: Bus bookings set to open as Dashain travel approaches
items.desc: Authorities are preparing to reopen damaged roads and ease the annual exodus of around 2 million people from Kathmandu Valley.

items.title: 12 dead in Baglung floods, landslides over past week
items.desc: The deaths occurred over several days as incessant rainfall triggered floods and landslides across the district, destroying 51 houses and damaging dozens of others.

items.title: Foreign minister meets UN General Assembly president, Sri Lankan counterpart
items.desc: Khanal discusses strengthening multilateralism with UNGA president and expanding bilateral cooperation with Sri Lanka.

items.title: US, Iran separately talk with mediators in latest bid to end war
items.desc: US and Iranian officials held separate talks with mediators as Washington and Tehran explored a renewed ceasefire effort, with further negotiations expected to focus on Iran’s seven-day proposal.
